solve_vie1(*, kernel, g=None, continuous=False, y0=None, dt=1.0, coll_setting=None, quadrature='product', samples_per_interval=None, kernel_interp_degree=None, mesh=None, coll_nodes=None, kernel_singularity=None, reuse_adaptive_blocks=True)

Solve a Volterra integral equation of the first kind.

\[g(t) = \int_0^t K(t-s)\, y(s)\, ds, \qquad 0 \le t \le T\]

by collocation: on each mesh interval \(y\) is a polynomial that satisfies the equation at the collocation nodes.

The inputs are either arrays of samples at \(t = 0, dt, 2\,dt, \ldots\) (the sampled regime) or callables (the functional regime, solved on the breakpoints mesh); see Notes.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default kernel array_like or callable

\(K\). Sampled: shape (N,), or (N, d, d) for a system of \(d\) equations, at \(u = 0, dt, \ldots, (N-1)\,dt\). Callable: kernel(u) returning a scalar or a (d, d) matrix; it may be vectorised over a 1-D u, which is faster.

required g array_like or callable

\(g\), with \(g(0) = 0\). Sampled: (N,), (N, d) or (N, d, m) for \(m\) right-hand sides. Callable: g(t) returning a scalar, (d,) or (d, m). Default zero.

None continuous bool

Use the continuous collocation method (Brunner's \(S_m^{(0)}\), degree \(m\) on \(m\) nodes, one order higher) instead of the default discontinuous one (\(S_{m-1}^{(-1)}\)). Needs y0 and a node at the right end of each interval.

False y0 array_like

\(y(0)\), for continuous=True only. Scalar, (d,) or (d, m).

None dt float

Sampled inputs: the sample spacing. Default 1.0.

1.0 coll_setting int or (int, sequence of int)

Sampled inputs: the collocation nodes choices / divs as (divs, choices), with choices in 1..divs, or a bare divs meaning every point 1..divs. divs also sets the mesh width (see samples_per_interval). Default (3, [1, 2, 3]).

None quadrature ('product', 'collocation')

Sampled inputs: how the integrals are evaluated from the samples. "product" (default) integrates a piecewise polynomial interpolant of the kernel exactly and accepts any mesh width and node set. "collocation" applies the interpolatory rule on the nodes; it is faster but fixes the mesh at divs**2 samples, runs only compiled settings (or the numba fallback), and is unstable when \(K(0)\) is small.

"product" samples_per_interval int

Sampled inputs: samples per mesh interval. A multiple of divs with product quadrature; default divs**2, because a first-kind inversion amplifies data errors by about the inverse of the mesh width. Must be divs**2 with collocation quadrature.

None kernel_interp_degree int

Sampled inputs, product quadrature: the degree of the kernel interpolant. Default: the number of nodes.

None mesh array_like

Callable inputs: the mesh breakpoints, strictly increasing from 0 to \(T\). Required for callable inputs.

None coll_nodes array_like

Callable inputs: node positions in \((0, 1]\), e.g. voles.radau_iia_nodes(3). Default [1/3, 2/3, 1].

None kernel_singularity (float, list, dict or callable)

Callable inputs: where the kernel is weakly singular, in \(u = t - s\): a location, a list of locations, {location: alpha} for \(K \sim |u - u_0|^{-\alpha}\) (enables Gauss–Jacobi rules), or a callable returning the singular \(s\)-locations for a time \(t\).

None reuse_adaptive_blocks bool

Callable inputs: on a uniform mesh, reuse adaptive-quadrature blocks across mesh intervals. Default True.

True

Returns:

Type Description VolterraSolution

The solution: sol.t and sol.y on the input grid (the samples, or the mesh breakpoints), sol(t) anywhere in \([0, T]\), plus the collocation data and coefficients.

Raises:

Type Description TypeError

An argument of the wrong type (a float where an integer is needed, a non-bool flag, a non-numeric array), or a required one missing.

ValueError

A wrong value: shapes that don't fit, an option from the other regime, a node set for which the method diverges, NaN or inf in the data, too few samples for one mesh interval.

NotImplementedError

Mixed callable and sampled inputs, or an uncompiled setting under quadrature="collocation" with no fallback.

LinAlgError

A collocation system is singular (e.g. an identically zero kernel).

Warns:

Type Description AccuracyWarning

\(g(0) \ne 0\); a node set with \(\rho = +1\) (one order lower); \(K(0)\) too small for collocation quadrature; a singularity declared on a uniform mesh.

PerformanceWarning

The numba fallback is used.

VolesWarning

A kernel_singularity location outside \([0, T]\).

  • solve_vie2, solve_vide: the other two equations.
  • VolterraSolution: the returned object.
  • optimal_graded_mesh: a mesh for a weakly singular kernel.
  • radau_iia_nodes: node sets for coll_nodes.
Notes

The regime is chosen by the input types: arrays give the sampled regime (dt, coll_setting, quadrature, samples_per_interval, kernel_interp_degree apply), callables the functional regime (mesh, coll_nodes, kernel_singularity, reuse_adaptive_blocks apply). The discontinuous method converges iff its amplification factor \(\rho_m = (-1)^m \prod_{i=1}^{m} (1 - c_i)/c_i\) satisfies \(|\rho_m| \le 1\), and the continuous one iff \(\rho_{m-1} = (-1)^m \prod_{i<m} (1 - c_i)/c_i\) does, with \(c_m = 1\) (Brunner 2004, Theorems 2.4.2 and 2.4.5). >>> import numpy as np
>>> import voles
>>> t = np.linspace(0, 2, 201)
>>> sol = voles.solve_vie1(kernel=np.ones_like(t), g=np.sin(t), dt=t[1])
>>> sol
<VolterraSolution vie1, sampled, 22 intervals on [0, 2], degree 2, ...>
>>> sol.y.shape
(201,)
>>> print(f"{sol(1.0):.6f}  {np.cos(1.0):.6f}")
0.540303  0.540302

...                        mesh=mesh, kernel_singularity={0.0: 0.5})
>>> print(f"{sol(0.25):.4f}")
0.5000

def solve_vie2(*, kernel: Data, g: Optional[Data] = None,
               dt: float = 1.0, coll_setting: CollSetting = None,
               quadrature: Quadrature = "product",
               samples_per_interval: Optional[int] = None,
               kernel_interp_degree: Optional[int] = None,
               mesh: Optional[ArrayLike] = None, coll_nodes: Optional[ArrayLike] = None,
               kernel_singularity: KernelSingularity = None,
               reuse_adaptive_blocks: bool = True) -> VolterraSolution:
    r"""Solve a Volterra integral equation of the second kind.

    $$y(t) = g(t) + \int_0^t K(t-s)\, y(s)\, ds, \qquad 0 \le t \le T$$

    by collocation: on each mesh interval $y$ is a polynomial that satisfies
    the equation at the collocation nodes.

    The inputs are either arrays of samples at $t = 0, dt, 2\,dt, \ldots$
    (the *sampled* regime) or callables (the *functional* regime, solved on
    the breakpoints ``mesh``); see Notes.

    Parameters
    ----------
    kernel : array_like or callable
        $K$. Sampled: shape ``(N,)``, or ``(N, d, d)`` for a system of $d$
        equations, at $u = 0, dt, \ldots, (N-1)\,dt$. Callable: ``kernel(u)``
        returning a scalar or a ``(d, d)`` matrix; it may be vectorised
        over a 1-D ``u``, which is faster.
    g : array_like or callable, optional
        $g$. Sampled: ``(N,)``, ``(N, d)`` or ``(N, d, m)`` for $m$
        right-hand sides. Callable: ``g(t)`` returning a scalar, ``(d,)`` or
        ``(d, m)``. Default zero.
    dt : float, optional
        Sampled inputs: the sample spacing. Default 1.0.
    coll_setting : int or (int, sequence of int), optional
        Sampled inputs: the collocation nodes ``choices / divs`` as
        ``(divs, choices)``, with choices in ``0..divs``, or a bare ``divs``
        meaning every point ``0..divs``. ``divs`` also sets the mesh
        width (see ``samples_per_interval``). Default ``(2, [0, 1, 2])``.
    quadrature : {"product", "collocation"}, optional
        Sampled inputs: how the integrals are evaluated from the samples.
        ``"product"`` (default) integrates a piecewise polynomial
        interpolant of the kernel exactly and accepts any mesh width and
        node set. ``"collocation"`` applies the interpolatory rule on the
        nodes; it is faster but fixes the mesh at ``divs**2`` samples and
        runs only compiled settings (or the numba fallback).
    samples_per_interval : int, optional
        Sampled inputs: samples per mesh interval. A multiple of ``divs``
        with product quadrature (default ``divs``, the finest mesh); must
        be ``divs**2`` with collocation quadrature.
    kernel_interp_degree : int, optional
        Sampled inputs, product quadrature: the degree of the kernel
        interpolant. Default: the number of nodes.
    mesh : array_like, optional
        Callable inputs: the mesh breakpoints, strictly increasing from 0 to
        $T$. Required for callable inputs.
    coll_nodes : array_like, optional
        Callable inputs: node positions in $[0, 1]$, e.g.
        ``voles.gauss_legendre_nodes(3)``. Default ``[0, 1/2, 1]``.
    kernel_singularity : float, list, dict or callable, optional
        Callable inputs: where the kernel is weakly singular, in
        $u = t - s$: a location, a list of locations, ``{location: alpha}``
        for $K \sim |u - u_0|^{-\alpha}$ (enables Gauss–Jacobi rules), or
        a callable returning the singular $s$-locations for a time $t$.
    reuse_adaptive_blocks : bool, optional
        Callable inputs: on a uniform mesh, reuse adaptive-quadrature blocks
        across mesh intervals. Default True.

    Returns
    -------
    VolterraSolution
        The solution: ``sol.t`` and ``sol.y`` on the input grid (the samples,
        or the mesh breakpoints), ``sol(t)`` anywhere in $[0, T]$, plus the
        collocation data and coefficients.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        An argument of the wrong type (a float where an integer is needed, a
        non-bool flag, a non-numeric array), or a required one missing.
    ValueError
        A wrong value: shapes that don't fit, an option from the other
        regime, an invalid node set, NaN or inf in the data, too few
        samples for one mesh interval.
    NotImplementedError
        Mixed callable and sampled inputs, or an uncompiled setting under
        ``quadrature="collocation"`` with no fallback.
    numpy.linalg.LinAlgError
        A collocation system is singular.

    Warns
    -----
    AccuracyWarning
        A singularity declared on a uniform mesh.
    PerformanceWarning
        The numba fallback is used.
    VolesWarning
        A ``kernel_singularity`` location outside $[0, T]$.

    See Also
    --------
    - [solve_vie1][voles.solve_vie1], [solve_vide][voles.solve_vide]: the other two
      equations.
    - [VolterraSolution][voles.VolterraSolution]: the returned object.
    - [optimal_graded_mesh][voles.optimal_graded_mesh]: a mesh for a weakly singular
      kernel.
    - [gauss_legendre_nodes][voles.gauss_legendre_nodes]: node sets for ``coll_nodes``.

    Notes
    -----
    The regime is chosen by the input types: arrays give the sampled regime
    (``dt``, ``coll_setting``, ``quadrature``, ``samples_per_interval``,
    ``kernel_interp_degree`` apply), callables the functional regime
    (``mesh``, ``coll_nodes``, ``kernel_singularity``,
    ``reuse_adaptive_blocks`` apply). An option from the other regime is
    an error. Mixing callable and sampled inputs is not supported yet.

    Examples
    --------
    Sampled data: $y(t) = 1 + \int_0^t y(s)\,ds$ has the solution $e^t$.

    >>> import numpy as np
    >>> import voles
    >>> t = np.linspace(0, 1, 101)
    >>> sol = voles.solve_vie2(kernel=np.ones_like(t), g=np.ones_like(t), dt=t[1])
    >>> sol
    <VolterraSolution vie2, sampled, 50 intervals on [0, 1], degree 2, ...>
    >>> print(f"{sol(1.0):.8f}  {np.e:.8f}")
    2.71828183  2.71828183

    Callables, on a mesh of your choice: $K(u) = e^{-u}$ and $g = 1$ give
    $y = 1 + t$, which the quadratic collocation polynomials represent
    exactly.

    >>> sol = voles.solve_vie2(kernel=lambda u: np.exp(-u), g=lambda t: np.ones_like(t),
    ...                        mesh=np.linspace(0, 1, 11))
    >>> sol.t.shape, sol.node_values.shape
    ((11,), (10, 3))
    >>> print(f"{sol(0.55):.6f}")
    1.550000
    """
    return _solve("vie2", kernel=kernel, g=g, dt=dt, coll_setting=coll_setting,
                  quadrature=quadrature, samples_per_interval=samples_per_interval,
                  kernel_interp_degree=kernel_interp_degree, mesh=mesh, coll_nodes=coll_nodes,
                  kernel_singularity=kernel_singularity,
                  reuse_adaptive_blocks=reuse_adaptive_blocks)

docs.title: VolesWarning
docs.text:
Bases: UserWarning

Base class of every warning voles emits.

Each diagnostic is issued once per solver call with warnings.warn, attributed to the line that called the solver, so the standard warnings filters apply. Python shows a given warning once per calling line by default.

See Also
  • AccuracyWarning, PerformanceWarning: the two kinds.

Examples:

A first-kind equation with \(g(0) \ne 0\) has no bounded solution, so voles warns. Make that an error:

>>> import warnings
>>> import numpy as np
>>> import voles
>>> with warnings.catch_warnings():
...     warnings.simplefilter("error", voles.AccuracyWarning)
...     voles.solve_vie1(kernel=np.ones(10), g=np.ones(10))
Traceback (most recent call last):
    ...
voles.AccuracyWarning: g(0) is not zero ...

or silence every voles diagnostic in a block:

>>> with warnings.catch_warnings():
...     warnings.simplefilter("ignore", voles.VolesWarning)
...     sol = voles.solve_vie1(kernel=np.ones(10), g=np.ones(10))
Source code in src/voles/_warnings.py 
class VolesWarning(UserWarning):
    r"""Base class of every warning voles emits.

    Each diagnostic is issued once per solver call with `warnings.warn`,
    attributed to the line that called the solver, so the standard
    `warnings` filters apply. Python shows a given warning once per
    calling line by default.

    See Also
    --------
    - [AccuracyWarning][voles.AccuracyWarning], [PerformanceWarning][voles.PerformanceWarning]:
      the two kinds.

    Examples
    --------
    A first-kind equation with $g(0) \ne 0$ has no bounded solution, so
    voles warns. Make that an error:

    >>> import warnings
    >>> import numpy as np
    >>> import voles
    >>> with warnings.catch_warnings():
    ...     warnings.simplefilter("error", voles.AccuracyWarning)
    ...     voles.solve_vie1(kernel=np.ones(10), g=np.ones(10))
    Traceback (most recent call last):
        ...
    voles.AccuracyWarning: g(0) is not zero ...

    or silence every voles diagnostic in a block:

    >>> with warnings.catch_warnings():
    ...     warnings.simplefilter("ignore", voles.VolesWarning)
    ...     sol = voles.solve_vie1(kernel=np.ones(10), g=np.ones(10))
    """
    __module__ = "voles"

docs.title: Plan: the 1.0 API (merged solver families + review fixes)
docs.text:
Status: all decisions settled 2026-10-31 (§2); the iterated solution is deferred to after 1.0. Phase 0 done 2026-10-31: - contract drafted in docs/dev/api-contract-1.0.md - battery docs/dev/api_battery.py: 510 cases, 3042 fields, 6 s; deterministic on re-run. Reference from 9ad2338: ~/.cache/voles_api_battery_9ad2338.npz. - benchmark baseline: ~/.cache/voles_bench_baseline_9ad2338.json (91 benchmarks)

Phase 0 findings: - (a) Bug: the callable family accepts a float coll_divs, e.g. 2.5 gives nodes {0, 0.4, 0.8} silently (_resolve_node_pos never checks the type of divs). Fixed in Phase 1 with F3. - (b) return_function=True never changes the sample values: values and rf_values agree bitwise in all 510 cases. So the new API can always request coefficients without breaking the wrappers' bitwise promise. - (c) The 0.10 API also accepts return_function=1, show_warnings="no", optimal_graded_mesh(M=10.0) and VIDE soln_init_value=None (both families). All F3/F5, fixed in Phase 1.

Phase 1 done 2026-10-31 (uncommitted at time of writing): - _warnings.py (3 classes; _warn walks frames to the caller) and _validate.py (integer/flag/real/choice/finite) - all 16 print sites converted, and matrix workers never warn - F3/F4/F5/F6/F17/F24 and bug (a) fixed; an invalid kernel_singularity no longer warns before raising - pytest filterwarnings = ["error"], with a voles_warnings fixture replacing capsys; new tests/test_validation_policy.py; 776 tests pass - battery vs 9ad2338: numerics bitwise identical in all 510 cases, warning texts unchanged, 41 strict mismatches, every one a deliberate error-type or rejection change - finite checks cost about 2 ms on a 660 ms matrix solve - CI on cf03239 then failed on two things the local setup (NumPy 1.26, warm numba cache) couldn't show: - Numba's NumbaPendingDeprecationWarning for a list coll_choices: fixed by passing an int64 array; - NumPy-2 scalar reprs in the non-finite message: fixed with Python scalars.

Both were verified in a scratch NumPy 2.5 / SciPy 1.18 / numba 0.68 venv with a cold cache: 890 tests pass.

Phase 2 done 2026-10-31: - VolterraSolution in _solution.py, exported, with the copy-free in-place Horner loop (bitwise equal to 0.10 off breakpoints; peak memory 134 → 43 MiB in a 400k-point matrix evaluation) - at_breakpoints with few-ulp snapping; to_ppoly(), complex supported - 0.11 deprecated aliases; legacy _SolutionFunction untouched; a genuine 0.10.0 pickle fixture in tests/data/ - adapters _from_legacy_sampled/_functional (removed in Phase 3) - tests/test_solution.py: 114 tests

Phase 3 done 2026-10-31 (lighter-engine variant): - _common.py holds 11 shared helpers; neither engine imports the other. - git mv to _sampled.py / _functional.py; voles/solvers.py is a re-export stub. - D1 renames of 12 private function names (_build_W_* → _build_w_*, solve_VIE_*_jit → solve_vie*_jit, …). The numba matrix builders A, BN, CN, G, … keep their maths names. - _samples_per_interval is the single mesh-width rule, used by the engine and by the entries. - The entries _sampled.solve / _functional.solve return a VolterraSolution, with a consistency check against the engine's mesh. The Phase 2 adapters became their builders. - New tests/test_engine.py (282 tests): bitwise identical to the engine across equations × quadratures × shapes × lengths × settings. - 1172 tests pass (NumPy 1.26, and NumPy 2.5 with a cold numba cache); the battery is unchanged; the strict docs build is clean.

Phase 4 done 2026-10-31: - _api.py: solve_vie1/2/vide with type hints and numpydoc (Examples come in Phase 6). Validation uses 1.0 names, in this order: 1. the regime is classified, with mixed inputs → NotImplementedError; 2. options from the other regime → ValueError; 3. coll_setting is resolved with the exact VIE-1 ρ rule; 4. mesh width and kernel degree, then shapes (2-D kernel reserved); 5. the matrix rule, with shared inputs broadcast (sampled) or g wrapped (functional); 6. compiled-setting checks.

It then calls _sampled.solve / _functional.solve. - _migrate.translate / describe: 0.10 call → 1.0 call; Phase 5 uses it for the deprecation messages. - Engine warning texts made API-neutral (17 battery text changes). - Builder trimmed (no vstack/tile, no copies of owned arrays; the mesh is still copied because it may alias the user's array). - Tests: - test_api.py (104): a table of invalid calls with expected types, and no 0.10 names in any message; - test_api_shapes.py (17): every matrix column equals its vector solve, including shared inputs; - test_api_equivalence.py (419): all 418 valid battery cases bitwise equal through the 1.0 API.

1711 tests pass (NumPy 1 and 2). - Overhead of the 1.0 path over the 0.10 return_function=True call: about 72 µs per call (N=82: 432 vs 360 µs; N=4001: about 2%). Revisit in Phase 7.

Phase 5 done 2026-10-31 (lighter-engine variant): - Engine functions renamed _sampled.vie1/vie2/vide and _functional.vie1/vie2/vide. Their recursive calls were renamed by AST position, so the docstring examples are untouched. - _legacy.py has the six wrappers with the exact 0.10 headers and docstrings, plus a deprecation notice. Each wrapper: 1. builds kwargs = dict(locals()); 2. warns once, using _migrate.describe of the non-default arguments; 3. calls the engine. - __init__ imports them from _legacy. - fast_coll_settings_* warn through a module __getattr__ and are out of __all__. - voles.solvers warns on import. - optimal_graded_mesh(t_end=, n_intervals=), with T=/M= deprecated. - return_polys now warns through _warn. - pytest ignores exactly the four 0.10 deprecation messages (pyproject), until the legacy tests, docs and benchmarks migrate. - The battery is unchanged except the two ogm message renames: 43 strict mismatches, all deliberate. - Parameters match v0.10.0 exactly, except _smooth_gl_order (F17). - _warn's frame walk is now cached per filename. abspath() was calling getcwd per frame; that cost 195 µs per deprecated call, and now 17 µs. - New tests/test_legacy_shims.py (30 tests); 1740 tests pass.

Phase 6 done 2026-10-31: - Cross-references: with griffe 2.2 / mkdocstrings-python 2.0.7 a numpydoc See Also is free Markdown; only autorefs [name][voles.name] link. The solver and class docstrings use that, as a list. - Runnable Examples on the three solvers, VolterraSolution, VolesWarning, optimal_graded_mesh and the node helpers (rounded output), run by tests/test_docstring_examples.py within the normal suite. The warning classes have __module__ = "voles". - User guide docs/guide/: conventions (regimes, shapes, nodes, the breakpoint table plus a Radau "left" demo, the VIE-1 noise table measured on the 1.0 API), warnings, migration, stability. - README, index, getting_started, all eight examples, the API pages (old URLs api/vie1/ etc. now show solve_vie1; the six 0.10 functions are on api/legacy.md), and the nav moved to the 1.0 API. - Deprecation messages: translated coll_nodes is shown exactly (np.array([1, 2, 3]) / 3, not rounded floats) and links the migration page. - Benchmarks call the 1.0 API with the same names; make_table.py labels. Measured overhead of the 1.0 path at small N: 175 vs 101 µs (vie1, N=500), 1936 vs 1796 µs (vie2, N=8000), mostly _from_sampled_engine and the coefficient request. That's for Phase 7. - CONTRIBUTING, CLAUDE.md and the CHANGELOG (Documentation section, the F34 extras notice, the breakpoint mean) are updated.

Phase 7 done 2026-11-01: - Performance. Overhead of the 1.0 path over the 0.10 values path, before → after, at N≈500: 60–74 → 41–49 µs; at N=8000, 140 → 68 µs. The fixes: - the sampled node arrays are built lazily (they cost 15–64 µs); - the exact VIE-1 ρ is lru-cached (Fraction arithmetic, three times per solve); - no defensive copy of the engine-built mesh.

Tried and reverted: a sum-based finiteness fast path. It needs np.errstate, which costs more than the isfinite it saves.

What remains is structural: the engine re-validates what _api already checked, the coefficient request costs 11 µs at N=500 (32 µs at 8000), and there's about 10 µs of object construction. Removing the double validation would need the check/run split of each engine function that the lighter-engine choice avoided. - F33: __version__ = "..." in src/voles/__init__.py is the source; pyproject has dynamic = ["version"] with [tool.hatch.version]. A wheel built and its metadata checked. (The dev env's editable metadata said 0.7.0.) - F30: aliases Data, CollSetting, KernelSingularity and Quadrature in _api; VolterraSolution attributes, properties, __call__ and to_ppoly are annotated, and its private state is declared. mypy is clean on _api, _solution, _warnings and __init__. tests/typing/public_api_usage.py (the documented calls) must run and type-check (tests/test_typing.py; mypy added to dev). pyright can't run on this machine (its Node build needs macOS 13.5), so there's no pyright CI step; py.typed waits for 1.0 as planned. - F32: tests/test_public_api.py and tests/data/public_api.json (regenerate with --update). - Benchmarks moved to the 1.0 API (held back from the Phase 6 commit). Inputs: docs/dev/api-review-1.0.md (34 findings, F1–F34) and the 2026-10-31 decision to merge the array-input and callable-input families.

docs.title: 1. Goal and shape of the result
docs.text:
Three public solvers replace six:

```python notest sol = voles.solve_vie2(kernel=K, g=g, dt=0.01) # sampled inputs sol = voles.solve_vie2(kernel=k, g=f, mesh=bps) # callable inputs sol.t, sol.y # the grid the problem was posed on, and the values there sol(t) # dense output sol.node_times, sol.node_values, sol.coefficients, sol.to_ppoly()


Two release steps:

- **0.11.0**: the new API, warnings through `warnings`, every bug-level fix,
  and the six old functions kept as deprecation wrappers. Each wrapper
  translates its kwargs, calls the new API, and converts the result back to
  the old return type. Old code keeps running with **bitwise-identical
  results**, with one accepted exception (dense evaluation at exact interior
  breakpoints, D5). Each wrapper call raises a `DeprecationWarning` that
  names the new call.
- **1.0.0**: delete the wrappers and other deprecated names, ship `py.typed`,
  and put the stability policy into force.

This matches the process agreed on 2026-10-12: deprecate in 0.11, remove in
1.0, with a signature-snapshot test as the guard.

**No D changes.** The D ABI already takes what both cores need. All the work
is in Python.

### Two input regimes, one documented rule

The cores stay two different discretisations, and the API says so in one
place instead of in the function names:

| | **sampled** | **functional** |
|---|---|---|
| Selected when | any of `kernel`, `g`, `a` is an array | all given inputs are callables |
| Grid argument | `dt` (sample spacing, default 1.0); the solver builds the mesh | `mesh` (breakpoints starting at 0, required); the user owns the mesh |
| Nodes | `coll_setting=(divs, [choices])` or `coll_setting=divs`: integers on the sample grid | `coll_nodes=`: floats in [0,1] ((0,1] for VIE-1) |
| Options that apply only here | `coll_setting`, `quadrature`, `samples_per_interval`, `kernel_interp_degree` | `coll_nodes`, `kernel_singularity`, `reuse_adaptive_blocks` |
| `sol.t` | the sample times n·dt, n = 0…N−1 | the mesh breakpoints |
| Core (today's code) | `solvers.py` internals + D | `_callable_solvers.py` internals + D/scipy |

- **Crossed inputs:** an option belonging to the other regime raises a
  `ValueError` that says which regime was inferred and why. Example: "kernel
  is an array, so the problem is sampled; mesh= is for callable inputs, use
  dt= and coll_setting=".
- **`dt` with `mesh`:** a `dt` other than the default, passed with `mesh`,
  raises. An explicit `dt=1.0` can't be told apart from the default and is
  ignored; this is accepted.
- **Mixed inputs** (e.g. a callable K with sampled g) are rejected in 1.0
  with `NotImplementedError`, and the contract doc reserves them. Adding them
  later breaks nothing. When added, their nodes sit on the sample grid, so
  they take `coll_setting`.

---

## 2. Decisions (settled 2026-10-31)

**D1. PEP 8 identifiers everywhere.**
- Public: `solve_vie1`, `solve_vie2`, `solve_vide`; `optimal_graded_mesh`
  parameters `T` → `t_end` and `M` → `n_intervals` (`alpha` and `order`
  stay).
- Private *function* names are renamed too (e.g. `_build_W_scalar` →
  `_build_w_scalar`).
- Maths-notation locals (`N`, `M`, `Q`, `K`, `W`, `K_real`) stay; PEP 8's
  "foolish consistency" clause covers them.
- The new names also make the deprecation clean: the old names keep their
  old return types throughout 0.11.

**D2. `dt: float = 1.0`**, sampled regime only. `mesh` is required in the
functional regime.

**D3. Nodes, one argument per regime.**
- Sampled: `coll_setting=(divs, [choices])`, exactly today's
  `coll_divs`/`coll_choices`.
  - A bare `coll_setting=divs` means every point the method admits: 1..q
    for VIE-1, 0..q otherwise.
  - `None` gives the default: VIE-1 `(3, [1,2,3])`; VIE-2/VIDE
    `(2, [0,1,2])`.
  - Any length-2 sequence is accepted. Integers only (NumPy ints allowed);
    floats raise `TypeError`.
  - The choices-only form is gone, which removes one of F22's three
    inference rules.
  - Why integers: `divs` also fixes the mesh. It is `divs²` samples wide
    under collocation quadrature, and it sets the default and the allowed
    multiples of `samples_per_interval` under product quadrature. So float
    node positions would lose information, and nudging a float could
    silently select an unrelated method.
- Functional: `coll_nodes=` floats, as today. `coll_setting` is *not*
  accepted there (F8: the same name must not mean two things). The
  defaults are the same node positions.
- `samples_per_interval` (renamed from `mesh_samples`) keeps today's rules:
  any multiple of `divs` under product quadrature, exactly `divs²` under
  collocation quadrature, and today's defaults.
- Docstring caveat: a bare `divs` with VIE-1 `continuous=True` gives
  ρ = (−1)^q, so for even q the method is admitted at reduced order, with an
  `AccuracyWarning`. Same as today's `coll_divs` alone.

**D4. VIE-1 continuous method: `continuous: bool = False` plus `y0`.**
`y0` is required when `continuous=True` and a `ValueError` otherwise (today
it is a printed warning). The initial value is called `y0` in all three
solvers (F13).

**D5. Returned object: one merged class, `VolterraSolution`** (§3). There is
no separate result-plus-solution pair: we have no solver diagnostics, since
failures raise, so everything the result would hold describes the piecewise
polynomial.
- **Breakpoint convention:** at interior breakpoints, `sol.y` and `sol(t)`
  report the *mean* of the two one-sided limits by default.
  `sol(t, at_breakpoints="left"|"right")` gives either limit.
- *Provisional:* revisit the default after the iterated-solution discussion.
- Measured error at interior breakpoints, K = e⁻ᵘ, y = cos t on [0,4]
  (scripts in that day's scratchpad, `breakpoint_sides*.py`):

  | Method | left | right | mean |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | VIE-1 default {1/3,2/3,1} | O(h³) | O(h³) | **O(h⁴)** |
  | VIE-1 Radau IIA p=3 | O(h³) | O(h³) | O(h³), best constant |
  | VIE-2 default {0,1/2,1} | O(h⁴) | identical (\|L−R\| ≈ 1e-16) | identical |
  | VIE-2 Gauss p=3 | O(h³) | O(h³) | **O(h⁴)** |
  | VIE-2 Radau IIA p=3 | **O(h⁵)** | O(h³) | O(h³) |

  Today the sampled grid output already averages (on both the D path and
  the product path), while `sol(t)` takes the right limit.
- **The 0.11 wrappers** take the new convention for dense evaluation at
  exact interior breakpoints. This was accepted as an accuracy improvement;
  on sampled VIE-1 data the error at breakpoints goes from 2.8e-7 to
  3.6e-9. *Superseded by the lighter engine (Phase 3/5):* the wrappers return
  the unchanged 0.10 object, so 0.10 dense evaluation doesn't change at all.
  `VolterraSolution`'s compatibility aliases were therefore dropped
  (`mesh_breakpoints`, `polynomials`, `len`, indexing, iteration). The class
  was never released, so no deprecation was needed.
- **`to_ppoly()` is added. `to_polynomials()` and the `Polynomial` list are
  removed.** The list survives in 0.11 only behind the deprecated
  `.polynomials`, indexing and iteration aliases.

**D6. `sol.t`/`sol.y` are the grid the problem was posed on.** That's the
sample times in the sampled regime and the mesh breakpoints in the
functional regime. The collocation data is `node_times`/`node_values` in
both regimes. The flattened `(M·p,)` node grid I first proposed is dropped:
with the default VIE-2/VIDE nodes it repeats every interior breakpoint,
which breaks `np.interp`/`searchsorted`.

**D7. Warnings:** `VolesWarning(UserWarning)` as the base, with
`AccuracyWarning` and `PerformanceWarning` under it.

| Site(s) | Category |
|---|---|
| ρ = 1 reduced order (`solvers.py:156`) | Accuracy |
| VIE-1 g(0) ≠ 0 (`:193`, `:197`) | Accuracy |
| VIE-1 K(0) small/singular, collocation quadrature (`:252`) | Accuracy |
| singularity declared on a uniform mesh (`_callable_solvers.py:2425`) | Accuracy |
| singularity location outside [0, T] (`:2417`) | base `VolesWarning` |
| Numba fallback (`solvers.py:744, 1387, 1650`) | Performance |
| stale D extension lacking the lag-block driver (`_product.py:605`) | Performance |
| `soln_init_value` ignored (5 sites) | becomes a `ValueError` (D4); a `VolesWarning` inside the wrappers until 1.0 |

**D8.** Mixed inputs are rejected in 1.0 and reserved (§1).

**D9.** Deprecations use `DeprecationWarning`.

**D10.** These names stay: `kernel_singularity`, `reuse_adaptive_blocks`,
`kernel_interp_degree`, `quadrature`. `mesh_samples` →
`samples_per_interval`. `optimal_graded_mesh(T=, M=)` is accepted with a
warning in 0.11.

**D11.** Every parameter stays keyword-only.

**D12. Non-finite inputs:**
- Arrays: raise `ValueError`.
- Callable `g` and `a`: checked at the collocation times.
- Kernel callables: not checked, and the docs say so. A singular kernel
  legitimately returns inf at u = 0, and the quadrature never samples there.

**Open: iterated solution.** For VIE-2, the iterated solution is
u_it(t) = g(t) + ∫₀ᵗ K(t−s) u_h(s) ds. It needs its own discussion:
- what it costs in each regime: in the sampled regime it's a convolution
  on the grid, like the residual prototype; in the functional regime it's
  a quadrature per evaluation point, and the result is not a piecewise
  polynomial;
- whether it is offered for VIDE, and what "iterated" means for VIE-1;
- what the API looks like (a method on `VolterraSolution`, or a solver
  option);
- whether it changes the `at_breakpoints` default.

The design below leaves room for it as an addition.

*Measured 2026-10-31* (brute-force quadrature on today's dense output; K = e⁻ᵘ,
y = cos t on [0,4], m = 3, M = 8→32; scratchpad `iterated_orders.py`,
`iterated_split.py`):

| Method | uₕ uniform | u_it uniform | u_it at mesh points |
|---|---|---|---|
| VIE-2 Gauss | 3 | 4 | ≥ 6 (reaches 1e-15 by M = 32) |
| VIE-2 Radau IIA | 3 | 4 | 5 |
| VIE-2 {0,1/2,1} (default) | 3 | 4 | 4 (= uₕ there) |
| VIE-2 {1/3,2/3,1} | 3 | 3 | — |
| VIDE Gauss | 4 | 6 | 6 |
| VIDE {0,1/2,1} (default) | 4 | 4 | — |

VIE-2: one extra order uniformly when κ ≥ 1, and order m+κ at mesh points.
VIDE with Gauss nodes: 2m uniformly. The rational node sets of the sampled
regime gain at most one order.

*Decided 2026-10-31:* the iterated solution comes **after 1.0**: functional
regime, VIE-2 and VIDE, as an additive `iterated=` keyword. The name is
reserved in the contract (§7), and the `"mean"` default stays.

---

## 3. Target public surface (0.11 additions; all that remains in 1.0)

```python notest
solve_vie1(*, kernel, g=None, continuous=False, y0=None,
           dt=1.0, coll_setting=None, quadrature="product",
           samples_per_interval=None, kernel_interp_degree=None,      # sampled
           mesh=None, coll_nodes=None,
           kernel_singularity=None, reuse_adaptive_blocks=True        # functional
           ) -> VolterraSolution

solve_vie2(*, kernel, g=None,
           dt=1.0, coll_setting=None, quadrature="product",
           samples_per_interval=None, kernel_interp_degree=None,
           mesh=None, coll_nodes=None,
           kernel_singularity=None, reuse_adaptive_blocks=True) -> VolterraSolution

solve_vide(*, kernel, a=None, g=None, y0,
           dt=1.0, coll_setting=None, quadrature="product",
           samples_per_interval=None, kernel_interp_degree=None,
           mesh=None, coll_nodes=None,
           kernel_singularity=None, reuse_adaptive_blocks=True) -> VolterraSolution

VolesWarning, AccuracyWarning, PerformanceWarning
optimal_graded_mesh(*, alpha, t_end, n_intervals, order)
gauss_legendre_nodes, radau_iia_nodes, lobatto_nodes
__version__

docs.title: VolterraSolution
docs.text:
Below, shape is () (scalar), (d,) (vector) or (d, m) (matrix). The dtype is complex for complex inputs.

Grid output. Each attribute means the same thing in both regimes.

Attribute Shape Sampled Functional t (K,) n·dt, K = N (computed on first access) mesh breakpoints, K = M+1 y (K, *shape) values from D, as today the mesh values, evaluated

Interior breakpoints use the mean convention. y is writable (users subtract exact solutions in place). Invariant: sol(sol.t) equals sol.y to rounding.

Piecewise-polynomial structure. Identical in both regimes; read-only unless noted.

Attribute Shape Meaning mesh (M+1,) breakpoints node_times (M, p) the actual collocation times, stored: on the sampled regime's final interval (Q+r samples) the nodes are snapped to that interval's own grid, so they can't be derived from mesh and nodes node_values (M, p, *shape) the collocation values (the unknowns). Functional: the solve output. Sampled: computed lazily from coefficients. Equals the old callable-family return. coefficients (M, P, *shape) local monomial coefficients in x = (t − tₙ)/hₙ ∈ [0,1]. This is the public accessor the noisy-data residual helper needs. nodes (p,) nominal node positions as floats coll_setting — (divs, [choices]) in the sampled regime, None in the functional regime equation — "vie1", "vie2" or "vide" regime — "sampled" or "functional" continuous — whether the space is C⁰: VIDE, or VIE-1 with continuous=True

Evaluation. - __call__(t, *, at_breakpoints="mean") returns (len(t), *shape), and a scalar t gives a scalar or a shape array (F20, documented). It returns NaN outside [0, T] (F21, documented). - at_breakpoints ∈ {"mean", "left", "right"} and only affects interior breakpoints. - Breakpoints are detected within a few ulps, because n·dt and n·(Q·dt) can differ by one ulp and exact equality would silently fall back to one limit. - At t = 0 only the right limit exists; at t = T only the left. - to_ppoly() returns a scipy.interpolate.PPoly: coefficients cₖ/hₙᵏ, highest degree first, trailing axes shape. That gives derivatives, antiderivatives, integrals and roots. PPoly evaluates right-continuously, and the docstring says so. Complex coefficients must be verified before promising them; if PPoly can't take them, raise TypeError for complex solutions. - __repr__ shows the equation, regime, interval count, T, degree, node set, shape and dtype. - Pickling works; lazy caches are not pickled. Pickles are not promised stable across minor versions; the stability policy says so. - No __len__, indexing, iteration, .polynomials, mesh_breakpoints or from_unit_coefs. These are deprecated aliases in 0.11 only.

Efficiency rules: - Nothing on the default path gets more expensive than today. In the sampled regime y comes from D unchanged. node_values and t are computed on first access. - Dense evaluation: a Horner loop indexing one coefficient at a time (c[idx, k]) instead of today's self._unit[idx] copy. That copy is (len(t), P, *shape), hundreds of MB for a matrix solution on a fine grid. The arithmetic order is unchanged, so the result is bitwise identical. - Coefficients are always produced. The D calls currently skip them when return_polys=False; Phase 7 measures the cost of always asking. I expect it to be negligible, since they are about N·p/Q, versus N for y. - Lazy caches are filled without a lock. That's a benign race, because the computations are idempotent.

docs.title: Shape and matrix-mode rule (F11, F19), stated once
docs.text:
• The time axis comes first.
  • The solution is matrix-valued exactly when some input has a column axis: sampled g (N,d,m), callable g returning (d,m), or y0 (d,m).
  • Every input with a column axis must have the same m.
  • An input without one is shared across all columns. This generalises VIDE's shared-(N,d) forcing to all solvers.
  • Complex inputs give complex outputs, and float32 is upcast.
  • A 2-D kernel array is rejected, which keeps it free for a future non-convolution K(tᵢ, sⱼ) (F25).

docs.title: Kernel convention (F25)
docs.text: A callable kernel is called with one positional array argument u and means K(t − s). A future non-convolution kernel will get a new keyword, never arity sniffing (which breaks on functools.partial, np.vectorize and numba dispatchers). Adding a keyword is non-breaking, so 1.0 only has to not promise arity-based dispatch.

docs.title: 4. Phases
docs.text: Each phase leaves pytest tests/ green, passes the bitwise battery (§5), and ends with an offer to commit. Phases 1–3 change no public signature.

docs.title: Phase 0: contract and baseline
docs.text:
1. Write the contract doc (docs/dev/api-contract-1.0.md; it becomes the user-facing conventions page in Phase 6). It covers:
  2. the regime rule
  3. the shape and matrix rule
  4. the breakpoint convention
  5. the kernel convention and reserved extensions
  6. the type/value error policy (F3: wrong type → TypeError, right type with a wrong value → ValueError; ints are numbers.Integral and not bool; bools must be bool/np.bool_)
  7. the warnings policy
  8. non-finite handling
  9. RuntimeError meaning "internal error, please report" (F4)
  10. the stability policy draft (F31)
  11. Baseline battery: generalise docs/dev/nogc_battery.py into docs/dev/api_battery.py, extended with:
  12. every old-API parameter combination (both families, all three solvers, scalar/vector/runtime-d/matrix/complex, both quadratures, continuous VIE-1, graded meshes, kernel_singularity forms, coll_nodes, a short final interval)
  13. the return_function coefficients and dense evaluation on a grid excluding exact interior breakpoints (the accepted D5 change)
  14. the exception type and message of a representative invalid call per validation branch

Save the reference from main before Phase 1. compare requires exact equality. 3. Benchmark baseline: run benchmarks/bench_solvers.py locally and keep the JSON. Small-N cases matter here, since the new validation layer is pure overhead there.

docs.title: Phase 1: foundations (no signature changes)
docs.text:
1. _warnings.py: the three classes and _warn(msg, category).
  2. stacklevel is computed by walking frames to the first non-voles frame. That's needed for Python 3.10/3.11; skip_file_prefixes only arrived in 3.12.
  3. Convert all 15 print sites (F1).
  4. show_warnings=False becomes an internal suppress flag checked inside _warn, not warnings.catch_warnings: that mutates process-global state and isn't thread-safe before 3.14, and the matrix path fans out to threads.
  5. The per-column recursive calls (e.g. _col_vie1 → solve_VIE_1 near solvers.py:1299) already pass show_warnings=False. Audit them so every warning is emitted once, from the calling thread (F2).
  6. _validate.py: one helper per parameter kind (integer, positive integer, bool, positive finite real, choice, 1-D increasing finite array starting at 0, array or callable, coll setting, …), each applying the F3 rule. Route _as_int, _check_time_step and friends through it. Behaviour changes, all for the changelog:
  7. coll_divs=2.0 raises TypeError
  8. time_step="0.1" raises a voles TypeError instead of the > comparison error
  9. show_warnings="no" and return_function=1 raise TypeError
  10. Phase 0 bug (a): _resolve_node_pos validates coll_divs as a positive integer (TypeError for 2.5 or 2.0), like the array family's _as_int. F5: soln_init_value=None on VIDE (both families) raises TypeError ("y0 is required").
  11. F4: _dlang.py:246 raises RuntimeError("internal error: <fn> returned code n; please report at <issues URL>"), listed in the Raises sections. Codes 1 (argument checks that Python already enforces) and 3 (too large, already a ValueError) are the only nonzero returns today.
  12. F6: the finite checks of D12.
  13. F17: move _smooth_gl_order to a module constant (_SMOOTH_GL_ORDER); only src/ uses it.
  14. F24: quadrature accepted case-insensitively.
  15. pytest: set filterwarnings = ["error"] plus explicit ignores, so every warning site must be expected with pytest.warns. Rewrite test_show_warnings.py from capsys to pytest.warns / recwarn, and add a test that a suppressed solve emits nothing from any thread.

Battery: numerics bitwise equal. The expected-exception table is updated only for the deliberate F3/F5 changes, each listed in the commit message.

docs.title: Phase 2: VolterraSolution
docs.text:
1. Build VolterraSolution (§3) in _solution.py from today's _SolutionFunction, plus:
  2. the grid output (t, y)
  3. node_times, node_values and the metadata
  4. at_breakpoints with tolerant breakpoint detection
  5. the copy-free Horner loop
  6. to_ppoly(), with complex support verified or refused explicitly
  7. __repr__
  8. 0.11-only deprecated aliases: mesh_breakpoints, polynomials (_polys_from_unit_coefs moves behind it), __getitem__, __iter__, __len__. Keep the legacy _SolutionFunction class unchanged in 0.11 so 0.10 pickles still load; delete it in 1.0.
  9. Internal constructor: VolterraSolution._build(raw, regime, equation, …) takes the cores' _Raw (Phase 3). Until Phase 3 lands, an adapter builds it from today's (values, _SolutionFunction) output.
  10. Tests:
  11. the invariant sol(sol.t) == sol.y (to rounding), in both regimes, for continuous and discontinuous methods
  12. the left/right/mean limits against direct polynomial evaluation
  13. breakpoint detection with ulp-perturbed t
  14. NaN outside [0, T]
  15. to_ppoly() against sol(t) away from breakpoints, plus its .derivative() against differentiated coefficients
  16. read-only flags; repr; a pickle round-trip
  17. the deprecated aliases warn
  18. a 0.10 pickle fixture loads

docs.title: Phase 3: separate validation from the cores (no signature changes)
docs.text:
Revised 2026-10-31 (Aaron chose the lighter engine): the six existing functions stay as a private engine, internal checks included; they are not split into normalise + pure core. Reading them showed validation interleaved with the dispatch tree (complex recursion, product vs collocation, matrix per-column recursion, vector vs scalar), so the split would be a rewrite of about 4,500 lines with every message to keep exact.

What Phase 3 does instead: 1. shared helpers move to _common.py, so neither core imports the other; 2. git mv to _sampled.py / _functional.py, with a voles/solvers.py re-export stub; 3. the D1 renames of private function names; 4. one engine entry per regime, _sampled.solve(equation, **engine_kw) and _functional.solve(...), returning a VolterraSolution. Its metadata (resolved setting, mesh width, final-interval nodes) comes from the same resolution helpers the engine uses, and is checked against the engine's mesh.

Consequences: - Phase 4's new API validates everything up front, with new names, so users never reach the engine's checks; the validation-table test enforces this. - Phase 5's wrappers call the engine directly, so the 0.10 API stays bitwise identical including error messages, which is better than the original plan. - Cost: two validation layers until 1.0, and the engine's unreachable messages keep 0.10 names until Phase 8.

The original text follows for reference.

This is the largest internal change. Today each public function validates and computes in one body (solve_VIE_1 is ~390 lines). After this phase:

  1. Move the shared helpers that the callable family imports from solvers.py (_column_workers, _check_vie1_setting, _warn_g_start_columns, _vie1_rho, …; see _callable_solvers.py:30) into _common.py, so neither core imports the other.
  2. git mv solvers.py _sampled.py and git mv _callable_solvers.py _functional.py, which keeps blame intact. voles/solvers.py comes back as a re-export stub; its deprecation is Phase 5.
  3. Split each of the six functions into normalise (validate, apply defaults, determine d/m/complex, produce plain arrays plus (divs, choices) or node_pos) and a core: _sampled_vie1(kernel, g, y0, dt, divs, choices, continuous, quadrature, Q, interp_deg, suppress) -> _Raw and its siblings.
  4. _Raw holds the grid values, unit coefficients, mesh, node times, node values (when the core has them), d and m, so all cores share one return type.
  5. The matrix fan-out and the complex block-embedding stay in the cores, so both API layers get them unchanged.
  6. Apply the D1 private-function renames in the same pass, while every call site is being touched anyway.
  7. The old public functions become normalise-old-kwargs → core → old return shape. This is a pure move. Battery: bitwise, including exception messages.

docs.title: Phase 4: the new API
docs.text:
1. _api.py: solve_vie1/2/vide with full type hints and numpydoc docstrings (Examples sections come in Phase 6).
  2. _classify(kernel, g, a) returns the regime, or a NotImplementedError for mixed inputs. callable() decides: an ndarray is not callable, while Polynomial, scipy interpolators, np.vectorize and numba dispatchers are.
  3. Regime-specific options per §1: dt/coll_setting/quadrature/ samples_per_interval/kernel_interp_degree versus mesh/ coll_nodes/kernel_singularity/reuse_adaptive_blocks. Wrong-regime options raise ValueError naming the regime.
  4. coll_setting resolution (D3): tuple, bare int or None gives (divs, sorted choices), then today's admissibility checks. coll_nodes validated as today.
  5. Shapes per §3 (matrix rule, shared inputs, 2-D kernels rejected).
  6. continuous/y0 per D4.
  7. Call the core and return VolterraSolution._build(...).
  8. Export the new names and warning classes from __init__. Leave the old names in __all__ for 0.11 so from voles import * keeps working.
  9. Tests (new files):
  10. test_api_regimes.py: classification, crossed options, dt≠default with mesh, mixed inputs.
  11. test_api_validation.py: a parametrized table of (call, exception type, message fragment). This makes the F3 policy executable.
  12. test_api_shapes.py: the matrix and shared-input rule across all three solvers and both regimes, plus complex inputs.
  13. test_api_equivalence.py: every battery case through the new API equals the old API bit for bit (y vs the old values; node_values vs the old callable return; coefficients vs the old unit coefs).
  14. test_api_solution.py: end-to-end VolterraSolution contents per regime, including node_times on a short final interval.

docs.title: Phase 5: old API to deprecation wrappers
docs.text:
1. Rewrite the six old functions in _legacy.py as kwargs translators onto the new API that convert the result back to the old return type:
  2. array family: sol.y
  3. callable family: sol.node_values
  4. return_function=True gives (values, sol); the VolterraSolution carries the 0.11 deprecated aliases for list-style access

Each emits one DeprecationWarning whose message is the equivalent new call, built from the actual kwargs, e.g. solve_vie2(kernel=..., g=..., dt=0.01, coll_setting=(2, [0, 1, 2])). return_polys and show_warnings keep working inside the wrappers only. 2. fast_coll_settings_* warn through a module-level __getattr__ (F16). There is no public replacement; _supported_coll_settings_d stays private. 3. voles/solvers.py: a stub that warns on import and re-exports the wrappers. 4. optimal_graded_mesh(T=, M=) is accepted with a DeprecationWarning (D1/D10). 5. Tests: - Existing test files keep calling the old API in 0.11. That way the whole legacy suite becomes wrapper coverage, and through the wrappers it exercises the new layer's numerics too. Each such file gets pytestmark = pytest.mark.filterwarnings("ignore::DeprecationWarning"). - New test_legacy_shims.py: every old kwarg is translated, every old return shape is reproduced, and each wrapper warns exactly once per call (not once per column). - The battery passes through the wrappers, bitwise (breakpoints excluded, per D5).

docs.title: Phase 6: documentation
docs.text:
1. Docstrings for the three solvers, VolterraSolution and the warning classes:
  2. a runnable Examples section on each (F27), doctested via --doctest-modules on src/voles (print rounded values so the doctests are platform-stable)
  3. See Also sections (F28)
  4. Raises split by TypeError/ValueError/NotImplementedError/ RuntimeError, plus a Warns section (F29)

First check which cross-reference syntax the installed mkdocstrings/griffe renders as a link (single backticks in See Also versus [name][voles.name] autorefs); don't assume. 2. New user-guide pages: - Conventions, from the contract doc: the regime rule, the shape contract (F19), the breakpoint convention with the D5 table and when to use "left", scalar t → scalar (F20), NaN outside [0, T] (F21), and why the VIE-1 default mesh is wider, with a worked example of the noise/discretisation trade-off (F23). - Warnings: the categories and how to filter or raise them. - Migration from 0.10: Appendix A, plus a before/after example per family. - Stability policy (F31): semver on __all__; numerical results may change in a minor release only as a documented accuracy improvement; deprecations warn for at least one minor release before removal; pickles are not stable across minor versions. 3. Rewrite README, getting_started.md, index.md, all eight examples pages and the mkdocs nav (API Reference becomes solvers / VolterraSolution / warnings / helpers). - examples/polynomial_solutions.md becomes "Working with the solution": coefficients, node_values, to_ppoly() (derivative, integral). - docs-examples.yml must pass. 4. benchmarks/bench_solvers.py moves to the new API but keeps its benchmark IDs, so the published history stays continuous. 5. Update the CLAUDE.md "Architecture" and "Dispatch flow" sections, and CONTRIBUTING. 6. CHANGELOG [0.11.0]: - the new API - the deprecations, with their removal version - the behaviour changes: prints become warnings, the ValueError → TypeError cases, VIDE y0=None, non-finite checks, and dense evaluation at exact breakpoints (mean of the limits) - an announcement that the [callable]/[numba] extras go in 1.0 (F34)

docs.title: Phase 7: guard rails and packaging
docs.text:
1. F32: tests/test_public_api.py pins voles.__all__ and the str(inspect.signature(...)) of every public callable and of VolterraSolution's public members against a checked-in snapshot.
  2. F30: full annotations on the public surface (ArrayLike, Callable[[NDArray], ArrayLike], Literal). py.typed is added at 1.0, once the loosely annotated wrappers are gone. Run a CI pyright --verifytypes voles (or mypy) check on the public surface.
  3. F33: make src/voles/__init__.py the single source of the version (pyproject dynamic = ["version"], [tool.hatch.version] path = ...). Update the release-procedure memory: version bumps happen in __init__.py.
  4. Performance check against the Phase 0 benchmark JSON:
  5. small-N overhead of the new layer
  6. the cost of always requesting coefficients from D (§3)
  7. dense-evaluation memory and time with the copy-free Horner loop

If anything regresses beyond noise, profile before release.

docs.title: Release 0.11.0, then a feedback window
docs.text:
• Follow the release procedure in the release-0-10-0 memory.
  • Write 3–4 "day-one" scripts as a new user would, using only the docs: a sampled VIE-2, a singular VIE-1 on a graded mesh, a matrix VIDE, a noisy-g VIE-1. Each awkward moment becomes an issue.
  • Ask William to port something real to 0.11, and collect what was awkward.

docs.title: Phase 8: 1.0.0
docs.text:
1. Delete:
  2. _legacy.py, the voles/solvers.py stub, fast_coll_settings_*
  3. the legacy _SolutionFunction
  4. the VolterraSolution deprecated aliases
  5. optimal_graded_mesh(T=, M=)
  6. the [callable]/[numba] extras (F34)
  7. Migrate the legacy test files to the new API. Mostly mechanical:
  8. kwarg renames by script
  9. coll_divs/coll_choices → coll_setting
  10. return_function unpacking → sol.y/sol.node_values/sol

test_function_solvers.py (264 call sites) is the bulk of it. Keep test_api_equivalence.py's reference outputs as a frozen .npz fixture, so coverage of the old numerics survives the wrappers' deletion. 3. Add py.typed, set the classifier to Development Status :: 5 - Production/Stable, regenerate the signature snapshot, and start the stability policy. 4. Release 1.0.0.

docs.title: 5. Verification and risks
docs.text:
• Bitwise battery (Phase 0 onward) is the main guard: the merge is a re-plumbing, and nothing numerical may move except dense evaluation at exact interior breakpoints (D5). Exception messages are compared too. Phase 3 especially has to keep the old messages exactly.
  • Breakpoint detection tolerance in __call__. Test with t perturbed by ±1–4 ulps, and with t = n·dt versus mesh = arange(M+1)·(Q·dt).
  • Final-interval nodes in the sampled regime: node_times must match snap_nodes exactly. Test with N chosen so that r = 1 and r = Q−1.
  • Warnings and threads: no catch_warnings on the solve path, and warnings are emitted only from the calling thread. test_threading.py gains a "warns once, from the main thread" case.
  • stacklevel must point at the user's call line through every layer (wrapper → API → core). Test it with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) and the recorded filename.
  • Error messages in the new API name new parameters. A wrapper user triggering a validation error sees the new name; the deprecation message printed just before shows the mapping, which is acceptable.
  • to_ppoly() with complex coefficients: verify before documenting.

docs.title: voles 1.0 API contract
docs.text:
Status: DRAFT 2026-10-31 (Phase 0 of docs/dev/api-1.0-plan.md). It becomes the user-facing "Conventions" and "Stability policy" pages in Phase 6.

This document is normative. Anything it promises is covered by the stability policy (§11) from 1.0.0 on, and anything it doesn't promise isn't. Where the implementation disagrees with it, the implementation has a bug or this document needs a decision; it is never silently resolved in favour of the code.

docs.title: 1. Public names
docs.text:
The public API is exactly the names in voles.__all__, their documented parameters and attributes, and voles.__version__:

Name Kind solve_vie1, solve_vie2, solve_vide solver functions VolterraSolution class of the solvers' return value (users never construct it) VolesWarning, AccuracyWarning, PerformanceWarning warning classes optimal_graded_mesh mesh helper gauss_legendre_nodes, radau_iia_nodes, lobatto_nodes node helpers

Anything else is private, including every module (all module names start with an underscore from 1.0), any name starting with an underscore, and the D extension's ABI. Importing the public names from submodules isn't supported; use from voles import ....

docs.title: 2. The three equations
docs.text:
With convolution kernels throughout (§7):

\[\text{VIE-1:}\quad g(t) = \int_0^t K(t-s)\,y(s)\,ds\] \[\text{VIE-2:}\quad y(t) = g(t) + \int_0^t K(t-s)\,y(s)\,ds\] \[\text{VIDE:}\quad y'(t) = a(t)\,y(t) + g(t) + \int_0^t K(t-s)\,y(s)\,ds,\qquad y(0) = y_0\]
  • Every parameter of every public function is keyword-only.
  • g=None means g ≡ 0, and VIDE a=None means a ≡ 0.
  • VIDE y0 is required, and y0=None raises TypeError.

docs.title: 3. Input regimes
docs.text:
Each solve runs in one of two regimes, determined by the types of the data inputs (kernel, g, and for VIDE a):

sampled functional Selected when at least one data input is an array (not callable) and none is callable every data input given is callable Grid dt (sample spacing, default 1.0). Inputs are samples at t = 0, dt, …, (N−1)·dt, where N is the kernel's length. The solver builds a uniform mesh of samples_per_interval samples per interval, with a longer final interval when the samples don't divide evenly. mesh, required: 1-D, finite, strictly increasing, mesh[0] == 0 Node set coll_setting (§5.1) coll_nodes (§5.2) Options that apply only here coll_setting, quadrature, samples_per_interval, kernel_interp_degree mesh, coll_nodes, kernel_singularity, reuse_adaptive_blocks

Rules:

  1. "Callable" means callable(x) is true. NumPy arrays are not callable; functions, numpy.polynomial.Polynomial, scipy interpolators, np.vectorize objects and numba dispatchers are.
  2. Mixed inputs (some data inputs callable, some arrays) raise NotImplementedError. The combination is reserved (§7), and its message says so.
  3. An option belonging to the other regime raises ValueError naming the inferred regime and the reason. That includes mesh in the sampled regime, coll_setting in the functional regime, and a dt other than the default in the functional regime. An explicit dt=1.0 alongside mesh is indistinguishable from the default and is ignored.
  4. VolterraSolution.regime records the regime (§8).

docs.title: 4. Solver signatures
docs.text:
```python notest solve_vie1(*, kernel, g=None, continuous=False, y0=None, dt=1.0, coll_setting=None, quadrature="product", samples_per_interval=None, kernel_interp_degree=None, mesh=None, coll_nodes=None, kernel_singularity=None, reuse_adaptive_blocks=True) -> VolterraSolution

solve_vie2(*, kernel, g=None, dt=1.0, coll_setting=None, quadrature="product", samples_per_interval=None, kernel_interp_degree=None, mesh=None, coll_nodes=None, kernel_singularity=None, reuse_adaptive_blocks=True) -> VolterraSolution

solve_vide(*, kernel, a=None, g=None, y0, dt=1.0, coll_setting=None, quadrature="product", samples_per_interval=None, kernel_interp_degree=None, mesh=None, coll_nodes=None, kernel_singularity=None, reuse_adaptive_blocks=True) -> VolterraSolution ```

VIE-1 method choice. - continuous=False (default): the discontinuous collocation space S⁽⁻¹⁾ₘ₋₁. Passing y0 then raises ValueError. - continuous=True: the continuous space S⁽⁰⁾ₘ, which needs the initial value: y0 is required (ValueError if missing). - The two methods admit different node sets (§5.3).

docs.title: 5.1 Sampled regime: coll_setting
docs.text:
Value Meaning None the default: VIE-1 (3, [1, 2, 3]); VIE-2 and VIDE (2, [0, 1, 2]) divs (int) every point the method admits: (divs, [1, …, divs]) for VIE-1, (divs, [0, …, divs]) otherwise (divs, choices) nodes cᵢ = choicesᵢ/divs; any length-2 sequence
  • divs is a positive integer. choices is a non-empty sequence of distinct integers in 0..divs (1..divs for VIE-1), in any order, and is sorted internally.
  • Python and NumPy integers are accepted. bool, floats (even integer-valued ones) and other types raise TypeError.
  • divs is not only the nodes' denominator: it also fixes the mesh (samples_per_interval below). Settings with the same node positions but different divs are different methods.

Mesh width (samples_per_interval, Q):

quadrature Allowed Q Default "product" (default) any positive multiple of divs divs² for VIE-1; divs for VIE-2 and VIDE "collocation" exactly divs² divs²
  • The VIE-1 default is wider because inverting a first-kind equation amplifies data errors by about the inverse of the mesh width. The Conventions page will carry a worked example of the trade-off.
  • kernel_interp_degree (default: the number of nodes) applies only to quadrature="product". With "collocation" it raises ValueError.
  • quadrature is matched case-insensitively.
  • The kernel needs at least Q+1 samples.

docs.title: 5.2 Functional regime: coll_nodes
docs.text:
• A non-empty 1-D sequence of distinct finite floats in [0, 1] ((0, 1] for VIE-1), in any order, sorted internally.
  • None gives the same positions as the sampled default: VIE-1 {1/3, 2/3, 1}; VIE-2 and VIDE {0, 1/2, 1}.
  • The node helpers return valid arrays, e.g. coll_nodes=voles.radau_iia_nodes(3).

docs.title: 5.3 Admissibility
docs.text:
• VIE-1 node sets must give a convergent method: |ρ| ≤ 1 with ρ = (−1)ᵐ ∏ (1 − cᵢ)/cᵢ for the discontinuous method, and the product over i < m for the continuous one. Otherwise ValueError.
  • The continuous method also requires c_m = 1.
  • ρ = +1 is admitted at one order lower, with an AccuracyWarning. A bare divs with continuous=True gives ρ = (−1)^divs, so this happens for even divs.
  • The ρ test is the only VIE-1 admissibility rule. It is evaluated exactly in rational arithmetic in the sampled regime, and in floating point for coll_nodes.
  • Only quadrature="collocation" depends on which settings are compiled into the extension (divs ≤ 4 in current builds); "product" accepts every valid setting. An uncompiled setting under "collocation":
  • scalar problems run on the numba fallback with a PerformanceWarning when numba is installed, and raise NotImplementedError otherwise;
  • vector and matrix problems raise NotImplementedError.

Both messages suggest quadrature="product". (Today's messages don't, and the scalar one points to fast_coll_settings_*; Phase 4 rewrites them.)

docs.title: 6. Shapes and dtypes
docs.text:
Time axis first, always. "Component shape" cs is () for scalar, (d,) for vector and (d, m) for matrix problems.

Input Sampled Functional (return value of the callable) kernel (N,) scalar, (N, d, d) vector/matrix K(u) → scalar or (d, d) g (N,), (N, d), (N, d, m) g(t) → scalar, (d,), (d, m) a (VIDE) (N,) or (N, d, d) a(t) → scalar or (d, d) y0 scalar, (d,), (d, m) the same
  • Matrix mode. The problem is matrix-valued exactly when some input has a column axis (g of (N, d, m) or (d, m), or y0 of (d, m)). Every input with a column axis must have the same m. An input without one is shared by all m columns. The columns are independent problems with a common kernel; they may be solved in parallel threads.
  • Callables must accept a scalar argument. The kernel is also tried with a 1-D array, and if it returns the leading-axis-stacked results it is used vectorised, which is much faster. g and a are currently called pointwise; a future release may vectorise them the same way, detected rather than assumed. Return shapes are detected by sampling.
  • Complex. Complex inputs (or callables returning complex values) give a complex solution. Real inputs give a real solution.
  • dtypes. Integer and float32 inputs are converted to float64 (or complex128). The output dtype is float64 or complex128.
  • Rejected arrays. A 2-D sampled kernel is invalid (reserved, §7). A sampled kernel of (N, d, d') with d ≠ d′ is invalid.
  • Non-finite values.
  • Arrays containing NaN or ±inf raise ValueError, naming the input and the first bad index.
  • Callable g and a are checked at the collocation times, with the same error.
  • Callable kernels are not checked: a weakly singular kernel legitimately returns inf at u = 0, which the quadrature never samples. Non-finite kernel values elsewhere give non-finite results.

docs.title: 7. Kernel convention and reserved extensions
docs.text:
• A callable kernel is called with one positional argument u (a scalar or 1-D array) and means K(t − s) evaluated at u = t − s ≥ 0. Kernel arity is never inspected.
  • Reserved, not promised. The following may be added in 1.x without breaking anything:
  • Non-convolution kernels K(t, s), through a new keyword argument. A 2-D sampled kernel is invalid in 1.0 so that it can carry this meaning later.
  • Mixed inputs: e.g. an analytic, possibly singular kernel with a sampled forcing, on the sample grid with coll_setting. These raise NotImplementedError in 1.0.
  • Iterated solutions: an iterated keyword for solve_vie2 and solve_vide, returning the iterated collocation solution u_it(t) = g(t) + ∫₀ᵗ K(t−s) uₕ(s) ds (and the VIDE analogue). The name iterated is reserved.
  • kernel_singularity declares weak singularities of the kernel (functional regime only). It accepts None, a location, a list of locations, a dict {location: alpha}, or a callable t ↦ locations; bools are rejected.
  • Locations in the first three forms are in u = t − s. In the dict form a non-None alpha ∈ (0, 1) declares K ∼ |u − u₀|^(−α) and enables Gauss–Jacobi rules.
  • The callable returns s-locations for collocation time t (an Abel kernel is lambda t: [t]), which anticipates non-convolution kernels.

docs.title: 8. VolterraSolution
docs.text: The solvers return a VolterraSolution, a continuous or discontinuous piecewise polynomial on mesh. Users don't construct it.

docs.title: 8.1 Grid output
docs.text:
Attribute Shape Sampled regime Functional regime t (K,) the sample times n·dt, n = 0…N−1 mesh y (K, *cs) solution values at t solution values at t
  • Invariant: sol(sol.t) equals sol.y to rounding.
  • y is writable; modifying it doesn't affect evaluation. t is read-only.

docs.title: 8.2 Structure (identical meaning in both regimes; read-only)
docs.text: Attribute Shape Meaning mesh (M+1,) breakpoints t₀ = 0 < … < t_M = T node_times (M, p) the collocation times actually used. On the sampled regime's final interval the nodes sit on that interval's own sample grid, so they can differ from mesh[n] + nodes·hₙ. node_values (M, p, *cs) the solution at node_times (the collocation values) coefficients (M, P, *cs) interval n's polynomial in the local variable x = (t − tₙ)/hₙ ∈ [0, 1], as monomial coefficients, lowest degree first nodes (p,) the nominal node positions in [0, 1], sorted coll_setting — (divs, choices) with choices a sorted list, or None in the functional regime equation — "vie1", "vie2" or "vide" regime — "sampled" or "functional" continuous — True when the solution space is C⁰ (VIDE; VIE-1 with continuous=True)

docs.title: 8.3 Evaluation
docs.text:
sol(t, *, at_breakpoints="mean"):

  • Shapes. A scalar t returns a Python float or complex for scalar problems and an ndarray of shape cs otherwise. An array t returns (*t.shape, *cs).
  • Domain. t ∈ [0, T] up to a rounding-level tolerance; points outside return NaN, never extrapolated values.
  • Breakpoints. At an interior breakpoint the two one-sided limits of a discontinuous solution differ. at_breakpoints chooses "mean" (the default), "left" or "right". A point within a few ulps of a breakpoint counts as that breakpoint. At t = 0 and t = T only one limit exists and is used.
  • Choosing a convention. "mean" is the most accurate of the three for most node sets. With VIE-2 and c_m = 1 (e.g. Radau IIA), "left" is superconvergent and better. The Conventions page carries the measured table.

sol.to_ppoly() returns an equivalent scipy.interpolate.PPoly (trailing axes cs). It is right-continuous at breakpoints and can differentiate, integrate and find roots. Complex solutions are supported (PPoly evaluates, differentiates and integrates complex coefficients; .roots() is real-only). Outside [0, T] it returns NaN, like sol(t).

docs.title: 8.4 Other behaviour
docs.text:
• repr(sol) is a one-line summary. Its exact text isn't part of the contract.
  • Solutions pickle. Pickles are not guaranteed to load in a different minor version.
  • No len(), indexing or iteration.

docs.title: 9. Errors
docs.text:
Exception When TypeError an argument has the wrong type, e.g. a float where an int is required, a non-bool flag, a non-callable where a callable is required in the functional regime, a non-numeric array, y0=None where y0 is required. Python's own TypeError for unknown or missing keywords. ValueError the type is right but the value is not: shapes, ranges, signs, inadmissible node sets, options from the other regime, inputs too short for the mesh, non-finite data, conflicting arguments NotImplementedError mixed inputs (§3); a setting that isn't compiled with no fallback for that problem shape (§5.3) numpy.linalg.LinAlgError a collocation system is singular or numerically singular ImportError the D extension can't be found or loaded RuntimeError an internal error. It always indicates a bug in voles, and its message asks for a report.
  • Type versus value rule. Integers are numbers.Integral but not bool. Flags are bool or numpy.bool_. Reals are numbers.Real but not bool. Arrays are anything numpy.asarray turns into a numeric array.
  • Integers aren't coerced. Floats are never truncated to ints (2.0 is a TypeError where an int is required), because silently running a different discretisation is worse than an error.
  • Messages name the offending parameter by its public name and, where useful, its value and the expected form. Message text isn't part of the contract.

docs.title: 10. Warnings
docs.text:
Class Base Emitted for VolesWarning UserWarning base class; also: kernel_singularity locations outside [0, T] AccuracyWarning VolesWarning ρ = +1 order reduction; VIE-1 with g(0) ≠ 0; VIE-1 with K(0) small or singular under collocation quadrature; a declared singularity on a uniform mesh PerformanceWarning VolesWarning the numba fallback; an extension build lacking a fast path
  • Warnings are emitted with warnings.warn. Each points at the user's call, is emitted at most once per solve call, and comes from the calling thread, never a worker thread.
  • warnings.simplefilter("ignore", voles.VolesWarning) silences all of them. "error" turns them into exceptions.
  • voles never prints. Third-party warnings (e.g. scipy's IntegrationWarning from adaptive quadrature) pass through unchanged.
  • The set of conditions that warn may grow in a minor release; new warnings are always VolesWarning subclasses.

docs.title: 11. Stability policy (from 1.0.0)
docs.text:
voles follows semantic versioning on the public API of §1.

  • Major releases may remove or incompatibly change public names, parameters, defaults, return types or attributes.
  • Minor releases may:
  • add names, keyword parameters with defaults, attributes and warning conditions;
  • change numerical results only as a documented accuracy or robustness improvement, named in the changelog;
  • deprecate. Deprecated features emit DeprecationWarning for at least one minor release before removal in the next major release.
  • Patch releases fix bugs only. A fix may change a result that was wrong.
  • Not covered: private names, message text, repr text, pickles across minor versions, the D ABI, performance (though regressions are treated as bugs), and bitwise reproducibility across platforms or builds.
  • Supported Python versions follow the classifiers in pyproject.toml. Dropping a Python version that is past end-of-life is allowed in a minor release.

docs.title: 12. Threads
docs.text:
• Solver calls are thread-safe. Concurrent calls from different Python threads give the same results as serial calls.
  • The extension releases the GIL during compiled work (ctypes.CDLL).
  • Matrix-mode solves may use a thread pool internally, sized to the column count and the CPU count.

docs.title: 13. Transition (0.11 only; removed in 1.0)
docs.text:
• 0.11.0 keeps solve_VIE_1, solve_VIE_2, solve_VIDE, function_solve_VIE_1, function_solve_VIE_2, function_solve_VIDE as deprecated wrappers.
  • Each call emits one DeprecationWarning showing the equivalent 1.0 call.
  • Each calls the 0.10 engine directly, so it returns exactly the 0.10 types, including the 0.10 solution object for return_function=True.
  • Results and error messages are those of 0.10, bitwise; dense evaluation is unchanged too.
  • Also deprecated in 0.11, all with a DeprecationWarning and all removed in 1.0:
  • fast_coll_settings_* (module attributes, no longer in __all__);
  • the voles.solvers module (warns on import);
  • optimal_graded_mesh(T=, M=), now t_end= and n_intervals=.
  • import voles and from voles import * emit no warnings.
  • Changes that affect 0.10 code directly, all listed in the 0.11 changelog:
  • warnings instead of prints
  • TypeError for wrong-type arguments
  • y0=None rejected in VIDE
  • non-finite data rejected
  • The migration table is in docs/dev/api-1.0-plan.md, Appendix A, and becomes the "Migration from 0.10" page.

docs.title: API review for 1.0 — inventory and first-pass findings
docs.text:
Reviewed against main at 3724a6a (v0.10.0), 2026-10-12. Scope: every name in voles.__all__, the object returned by return_function=True, and the error and warning behaviour observable from Python. Not reviewed: internal modules, the D ABI, docs prose beyond what the public functions promise.

The benchmark throughout is "would this pass review as scipy.integrate.solve_X": keyword-only, a result object with named fields, numpydoc docstrings with runnable examples, errors and warnings through the standard channels, and a written stability promise.
